rv.q: Benne has crafted two memorable, sympathetic characters whose mutual love holds them together in the face of very real fears, and Corona and Colón shine in these roles.
Benjamin Benne has delivered a beautiful one-act drama that’s actually about so many present day issues.
From start to finish, the moving world premiere of “Alma,” commands the intimate stage at the Rivendell Theatre in Edgewater.
In the end, this is a love story between a mother and her daughter, and that works in any language.
This is a big-hearted, high-caliber production shoehorned into a small space, and it shows just what storefront theater is capable of in terms of intimacy and impact.
Alma has impact, and it will keep you engaged.
You should find this to be a "think piece"!
With heartfelt direction by Ana Velazquez, Alma finds power in the bond between mother and daughter.

cn.t: Benjamin Benne's powerful world premiere earns praise for its poignant exploration of immigration and the American Dream through a compelling mother-daughter relationship, with critics highlighting strong performances and relevant storytelling.
